summary.one_liner: CAMEL is an open-source Python framework and research community for building and studying multi-agent systems, with tools for agents, tasks, models, and simulated environments.
summary.what_it_does: CAMEL provides building blocks for LLM-based agents, including ChatAgent, agent societies, models, tools, memory, storage, retrievers, and interpreters, as listed in its Tech Stack table. The README's quick start shows creating a ChatAgent with a model from ModelFactory and a DuckDuckGo search tool from SearchToolkit. The project describes itself as aimed at research on the scaling laws of agents, and it lists use areas including data generation, task automation, and world simulation. It also includes synthetic datasets hosted on Hugging Face, cookbooks covering RAG, graph RAG, memory, tools, and fine-tuning workflows, and a set of real-world use cases. Optional environment variables enable JSON logging of model requests and responses.
use_cases: build a multi-agent system in Python
generate synthetic training data with LLMs
create a chat agent with web search tools
how_to_run: Create a ChatAgent with ModelFactory and SearchToolkit().search_duckduckgo as a tool, then call agent.step(...)
notable: Covers agent societies, synthetic data generation, and simulated environments in one framework
Large cookbook and real-world use case collection with RAG, graph RAG, and fine-tuning examples
Optional JSON logging of model requests and responses with UTF-8 output
Community-driven research collective with 100+ researchers, per the README
caveats: Quick start uses OpenAI by default and requires an API key; other providers are configured through the ModelFactory
Some features are installed as optional extras such as web_tools, so the base install may not include everything
Installation details are deferred to the docs site and installation section, which are not included in this README
